decisions.choice: a man, one, a man, one, from a tribe: one man from each tribe

decisions.choice: firmly: the priests' feet stood fixed in one place
alternatives: take up twelve stones that have been made ready
the place where the priests' feet were set
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning "to make firm" or "to make ready". The same form in 3:17 says the priests stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, and that is the sense taken here. The accents of the Hebrew text join the word to what follows, which allows another reading: "prepare twelve stones", that is, have them made ready to carry.

decisions.choice: the lodging place: the place where the people would spend that night, at Gilgal
decisions.reason: The word names a place to stop for the night, such as a traveler's camp (Genesis 42:27). The people camp that night at Gilgal (verses 19-20), and the stones are set up there.

decisions.choice: for yourselves: a plural command to the twelve men
decisions.reason: From here on the command is spoken to the twelve men themselves, each of whom is to carry one stone (verse 5).

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the words the men are to hear
decisions.reason: The LORD's words to Joshua open with double quotation marks in verse 2. The command Joshua is to pass on is a quotation inside them, so it takes single marks, and both close at the end of this verse.

decisions.choice: right where the priests are standing
decisions.reason: Readable leaves the idea of standing "firm" in the plain word "standing", since the priests have not moved from the spot (verse 10).

decisions.choice: the twelve men addressed as "các ông" in the words Joshua is to pass on
decisions.reason: Joshua is to speak to twelve leading men chosen from the tribes; "các ông" is the respectful plural for grown men. Literal keeps "các ngươi", as for God's own words.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the words the twelve men are to hear inside the LORD's speech
decisions.reason: Korean, like the English, marks a quotation inside a quotation with single marks, as the style guide sets.

en.L: And Joshua said to them, "Cross over before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God into the middle of the Jordan, and lift up for yourselves, each man, one stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel,
en.B: Joshua said to them, "Go ahead of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, out to the middle of the Jordan. Every one of you is to lift a stone onto his shoulder, one for each of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}},
en.R: Joshua told them, "Go out into the middle of the Jordan, in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Each of you must pick up a stone and carry it on your shoulder. There must be one stone for each tribe of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

sw.L: Yoshua akawaambia, "Vukeni mbele ya sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu hadi katikati ya Yordani, na kila mtu ajitwike jiwe moja begani mwake, kwa hesabu ya makabila ya wana wa Israeli,

sw.R: Yoshua aliwaambia, "Nendeni katikati ya Yordani, mbele ya sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu. Kila mmoja wenu lazima achukue jiwe na kulibeba begani. Liwe jiwe moja kwa kila kabila la Waisraeli.

es.L: Y Josué les dijo: «{{plural_you:Pasen|Pasad}} delante del arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} hasta el medio del Jordán, y {{plural_you:alcen|alzad}} cada uno una piedra sobre su hombro, conforme al número de las tribus de los hijos de Israel,
es.B: Josué les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} delante del arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} hasta el medio del Jordán. Cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cargará una piedra sobre su hombro, una por cada tribu de los israelitas,
es.R: Josué les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} hasta el medio del Jordán, delante del arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}. Cada uno tiene que levantar una piedra y llevarla sobre el hombro. Tiene que haber una piedra por cada tribu de los israelitas.

fr.L: Et Josué leur dit : « Passez devant l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu jusqu’au milieu du Jourdain, et soulevez-vous chacun une pierre sur son épaule, selon le nombre des tribus des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël,
fr.B: Josué leur dit : « Avancez devant l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu jusqu’au milieu du Jourdain. Que chacun de vous charge une pierre sur son épaule, une pour chacune des tribus des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}},
fr.R: Josué leur a dit : « Allez au milieu du Jourdain, devant l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu. Chacun de vous doit ramasser une pierre et la porter sur son épaule. Il faut une pierre pour chaque tribu des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}.

vi.L: Và Giô-suê nói với họ: "Hãy đi qua trước hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời các ngươi vào giữa sông Giô-đanh, và mỗi người hãy vác một hòn đá trên vai mình, theo số các chi tộc của con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên,
vi.B: Giô-suê bảo họ: "Hãy đi trước hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của các ông, ra đến giữa sông Giô-đanh. Mỗi người hãy vác một hòn đá lên vai, mỗi hòn cho một chi tộc của dân Y-sơ-ra-ên,
vi.R: Giô-suê bảo họ: "Hãy đi ra giữa sông Giô-đanh, đến trước hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của các ông. Mỗi người phải lấy một hòn đá và vác trên vai. Phải có một hòn đá cho mỗi chi tộc của dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 여호수아가 그들에게 말했다. "너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤 앞으로 요단 한가운데로 건너가서, 이스라엘 자손 지파의 수대로 너희가 각각 돌 하나씩을 어깨에 메어라.
ko.B: 여호수아가 그들에게 말했다. "너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤 앞으로 나아가 요단강 한가운데로 들어가거라. 너희는 각각 돌 하나씩을 어깨에 메어라. 이스라엘 자손의 지파마다 하나씩이다.
ko.R: 여호수아가 그들에게 말했다. "너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤 앞으로 가서 요단강 한가운데로 들어가거라. 너희는 저마다 돌 하나를 집어 어깨에 메고 오너라. 이스라엘 백성의 지파마다 돌이 하나씩 있어야 한다.

decisions.choice: cross over before the ark: go out into the riverbed, to where the ark stands
decisions.reason: The people have already crossed (verse 1), and the ark is still in the middle of the river with the priests (verse 10). The twelve men go back out from the bank, passing in front of the ark, to take stones from the spot where the priests are standing (verse 3).

decisions.choice: one stone on his shoulder: a large stone, each one a load for a man
decisions.reason: Each stone was big enough that a man had to carry it on his shoulder. Set up together, they would make a monument people could see (verse 20).

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 6
decisions.reason: Joshua's command and its purpose ("so that this may be a sign") are one sentence in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: There must be one stone for each tribe
decisions.reason: Readable ends the command here and starts the purpose as a new sentence in verse 6, so the sentences stay short.

pt.B: para que isto seja um sinal entre vocês. No futuro, quando os filhos de vocês perguntarem: 'Que significam estas pedras para vocês?'
pt.R: Estas pedras vão ser um sinal para vocês. Um dia os filhos de vocês vão perguntar: 'O que significam estas pedras?'

decisions.choice: a sign: something to see that points to what God has done
decisions.reason: A "sign" here is a reminder that can be seen and that calls for an explanation, like the Passover meal and the feast of unleavened bread (Exodus 13:9) or the twelve stones of the altar at Sinai (Exodus 24:4).

decisions.choice: tomorrow: in time to come
decisions.reason: "Tomorrow" here means any day in the future, as in Exodus 13:14 and Deuteronomy 6:20.

decisions.choice: the question of the children: the way the law teaches the next generation
decisions.reason: The pattern of a child asking and a parent explaining is the pattern of the Passover (Exodus 12:26-27; 13:14) and of the law as a whole (Deuteronomy 6:20-25). The stones will open the same kind of conversation.

decisions.choice: What do these stones mean (to you)?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "What are these stones to you?" asks what they stand for. Balanced and Readable put it as English asks it.

decisions.choice: children, with "sons" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of "son", but here it means the next generation, girls as well as boys.

decisions.choice: "watoto" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span "watoto|wana", as the English "children|sons"
decisions.reason: "Watoto" already means sons and daughters, and is the plain word for children asking their parents; "wana" says the same, so there is no second wording for the setting to change. Where the English has "parents|fathers" (verse 21), Swahili does have two wordings, "wazazi" and "baba", and keeps the span.

decisions.choice: "hijos" with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already takes in daughters as well as sons, so the gender setting the English has here ("children" or "sons") is not needed; the same holds for "padres" (parents) in verse 21.

decisions.choice: "con cái" with no gender span
alternatives: a span between "con cái" and "con trai"
decisions.reason: "con cái" means sons and daughters alike and is what Vietnamese says here; the English needs a setting for "children" or "sons", Vietnamese does not. The children's "you" is "cha mẹ" (L, B), as Vietnamese children address their parents.

decisions.choice: a gender setting span with "자녀들" by default and "아들들" as the alternative
decisions.reason: Here Korean has two real wordings, "자녀들" (children) and the Hebrew's "아들들" (sons), so the gender setting chooses between them, as the English does. Both end the same way, so the particle stands outside the span.

decisions.choice: os filhos de vocês, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a setting to choose between "children" and "sons". Portuguese "filhos" already means children, girls as well as boys, as the meaning here asks (r-en-2), so there is nothing for a setting to change; the same in verses 21-22.

ko.R: 그러면 너희는 이렇게 말해 주어라. '{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 언약궤 앞에서 요단강 물이 흐르기를 멈추었단다. 그 궤가 강을 건널 때에 물이 멈추었단다.' 이 돌들은 이스라엘 백성이 그때 일어난 일을 언제까지나 기억하게 해 줄 것이다."

pt.L: então vocês lhes dirão que as águas do Jordão foram cortadas diante da arca da aliança {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; quando ela passou pelo Jordão, as águas do Jordão foram cortadas. E estas pedras serão por memorial para os filhos de Israel para sempre."
pt.B: então digam a eles: 'Diante da arca da aliança {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} as águas do Jordão foram cortadas. Quando ela entrou no Jordão, as águas do Jordão foram cortadas.' Estas pedras serão um memorial para os israelitas para sempre."
pt.R: Então vocês vão dizer a eles: 'A água do Jordão parou de correr diante da arca da aliança {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Quando a arca atravessou o rio, a água parou.' Estas pedras vão ajudar os israelitas a lembrar para sempre o que aconteceu."

decisions.choice: were cut off: stopped flowing and were held back
decisions.reason: The verb means "to cut" or "to cut off". Said of a river, it means the flow was stopped, as 3:13 and 3:16 describe: the water coming down stood up in a heap far upstream, and the water below ran off to the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: the words "were cut off" are said twice for emphasis
decisions.reason: The answer repeats the main fact, first with the ark ("before the ark") and then with the moment ("when it crossed"). The repetition stresses that the ark of the covenant, the sign of God's presence, is what stopped the river.

decisions.choice: memorial: a reminder that keeps an event in the people's memory
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to remember". A memorial calls something to mind for the people and before God (Exodus 12:14; 28:12; Numbers 17:5 in the Hebrew numbering).

decisions.choice: the answer to the children ends with "cut off"; the last sentence is Joshua's word to the men
alternatives: the parents' answer runs to the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no quotation marks. The answer the parents are to give is the account of the waters; the closing words about a memorial "forever" read as Joshua's own statement of what the stones are for. They could also be taken as part of the answer.

decisions.choice: direct quotation for "that ..."
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "say to them that ...". Balanced and Readable give the parents' answer as their own words, in single quotation marks inside Joshua's speech.

decisions.choice: will always help ... remember what happened
decisions.reason: Readable explains "memorial" by what it does, and says "always" for "until forever".

decisions.choice: the parents' answer to their children in the plain style; Readable uses the gentle "-단다" a parent uses to a child
decisions.reason: Parents speak to children in the plain style, as the terms of this translation set; at Readable the child's question and the parent's answer use the everyday forms of a family conversation.

decisions.choice: "vật kỷ niệm"
decisions.reason: A memorial is a reminder that keeps the event in the people's memory (m3). "vật kỷ niệm" says that plainly; "đài tưởng niệm" would suggest a built monument.

source.text: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֣ן בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֘לכַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֒ וַיִּשְׂא֡וּ שְׁתֵּֽי־עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה אֲבָנִ֜ים מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּ֗ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ לְמִסְפַּ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּעֲבִר֤וּם עִמָּם֙ אֶל־הַמָּל֔וֹן וַיַּנִּח֖וּם שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And did so [the] sons of Israel just as commanded Joshua, and they lifted up twelve stones from [the] middle of the Jordan, just as spoke Yahweh to Joshua, according to [the] number of [the] tribes of [the] sons of Israel; and they carried them over with them to the lodging place and set them down there.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did so, just as Joshua commanded, and they lifted up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; and they carried them over with them to the lodging place and set them down there.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did as Joshua commanded. They lifted twelve stones out of the middle of the Jordan, one for each of the tribes of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Joshua. They took them across to the camping place and laid them down there.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what Joshua told them. Just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Joshua, they took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, one stone for every tribe of Israel. They carried the stones to the place where they camped for the night and put them down there.

sw.L: Wana wa Israeli wakafanya hivyo, kama Yoshua alivyoamuru, wakainua mawe kumi na mawili kutoka katikati ya Yordani, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwambia Yoshua, kwa hesabu ya makabila ya wana wa Israeli; wakayavusha pamoja nao hadi mahali pa kulala, wakayaweka huko.
sw.B: Waisraeli walifanya kama Yoshua alivyoamuru. Waliinua mawe kumi na mawili kutoka katikati ya Yordani, moja kwa kila kabila la Waisraeli, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwambia Yoshua. Wakayavusha hadi mahali pa kambi, wakayaweka chini huko.
sw.R: Waisraeli walifanya kama Yoshua alivyowaambia. Kama vile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amemwambia Yoshua, walichukua mawe kumi na mawili kutoka katikati ya Yordani, jiwe moja kwa kila kabila la Israeli. Wakayabeba mpaka mahali walipolala usiku ule, wakayaweka chini huko.

es.L: Y los hijos de Israel lo hicieron así, tal como Josué mandó, y alzaron doce piedras de en medio del Jordán, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho a Josué, conforme al número de las tribus de los hijos de Israel; y las llevaron consigo al lugar donde pasaron la noche y las pusieron allí.
es.B: Los israelitas hicieron lo que Josué mandó. Sacaron doce piedras de en medio del Jordán, una por cada tribu de los israelitas, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había dicho a Josué. Las llevaron al lugar donde acamparon y las dejaron allí.
es.R: Los israelitas hicieron lo que Josué les dijo. Tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había dicho a Josué, sacaron doce piedras de en medio del Jordán, una piedra por cada tribu de Israel. Llevaron las piedras al lugar donde acamparon esa noche y las pusieron allí.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël firent ainsi, comme Josué l’avait commandé, et ils soulevèrent douze pierres du milieu du Jourdain, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait dit à Josué, selon le nombre des tribus des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël ; et ils les emportèrent avec eux au lieu de halte et les y déposèrent.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} firent ce que Josué avait ordonné. Ils retirèrent douze pierres du milieu du Jourdain, une pour chacune des tribus des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait dit à Josué. Ils les emportèrent jusqu’au campement et les y déposèrent.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont fait ce que Josué leur avait dit. Comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait dit à Josué, ils ont pris douze pierres au milieu du Jourdain, une pierre pour chaque tribu d’Israël. Ils ont porté les pierres jusqu’à l’endroit où ils ont campé pour la nuit et les ont posées là.

vi.L: Và con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên làm như vậy, đúng như Giô-suê đã truyền, và họ lấy mười hai hòn đá từ giữa sông Giô-đanh, đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán với Giô-suê, theo số các chi tộc của con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên; và họ đem chúng theo qua đến nơi nghỉ và đặt chúng tại đó.
vi.B: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm đúng như Giô-suê truyền. Họ lấy mười hai hòn đá từ giữa sông Giô-đanh, mỗi hòn cho một chi tộc của dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán với Giô-suê. Họ mang các hòn đá qua đến nơi đóng trại và đặt xuống tại đó.
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên làm đúng như Giô-suê bảo. Đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán với Giô-suê, họ lấy mười hai hòn đá từ giữa sông Giô-đanh, mỗi chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên một hòn. Họ mang các hòn đá đến nơi họ đóng trại qua đêm và đặt xuống đó.

ko.L: 그러자 이스라엘 자손이 여호수아가 명령한 대로 그렇게 했다. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 여호수아에게 말씀하신 대로, 이스라엘 자손 지파의 수대로 요단 한가운데에서 돌 열두 개를 들어 올렸고, 그것들을 자기들과 함께 묵을 곳으로 가지고 건너가서 거기에 내려놓았다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 자손은 여호수아가 명령한 대로 했다. 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 여호수아에게 말씀하신 대로 요단강 한가운데에서 이스라엘 자손의 지파마다 하나씩 돌 열두 개를 들어 올렸다. 그리고 그 돌들을 진을 칠 곳으로 가지고 건너가서 거기에 내려놓았다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성은 여호수아가 말한 대로 했다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 여호수아에게 말씀하신 대로, 그들은 요단강 한가운데에서 돌 열두 개를 가져왔다. 이스라엘의 지파마다 돌이 하나씩이었다. 그들은 그 돌들을 그날 밤 묵을 곳으로 가져가서 거기에 내려놓았다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Israel fizeram assim, como Josué ordenou, e levantaram doze pedras do meio do Jordão, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha falado a Josué, conforme o número das tribos dos filhos de Israel; e as levaram com eles para o lugar de pernoite e as depuseram ali.
pt.B: Os israelitas fizeram como Josué ordenou. Tiraram doze pedras do meio do Jordão, uma para cada tribo dos israelitas, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha dito a Josué. Levaram-nas até o lugar do acampamento e as colocaram ali.
pt.R: Os israelitas fizeram o que Josué mandou. Como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha dito a Josué, eles tiraram doze pedras do meio do Jordão, uma pedra para cada tribo de Israel. Levaram as pedras até o lugar onde acamparam para passar a noite e as colocaram ali.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel did so: the whole people acted through the twelve men
decisions.reason: The twelve men did the carrying (verse 5), but the verse says "the sons of Israel" did it. Each man stood for his tribe, so what they did, all Israel did.

decisions.choice: just as Joshua commanded ... just as the LORD had spoken: Joshua's order carries the LORD's word
decisions.reason: The verse names both: the people obey Joshua, and in doing so they do what the LORD told Joshua (verses 1-3). Verse 10 adds Moses to the chain, and the chapter shows Joshua as a leader whose word can be trusted because it comes from God (verse 14).

decisions.choice: one for each of the tribes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable move "according to the number of the tribes" next to "twelve stones", where it belongs in English, and say it as "one for each".

source.text: וּשְׁתֵּ֧ים עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אֲבָנִ֗ים הֵקִ֣ים יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֮ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּן֒ תַּ֗חַת מַצַּב֙ רַגְלֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים נֹשְׂאֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן הַבְּרִ֑ית וַיִּ֣הְיוּ שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And twelve stones set up Joshua in [the] middle of the Jordan, in place of [the] standing place of [the] feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant; and they have been there until the day the this.

en.L: And twelve stones Joshua set up in the middle of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant had stood; and they have been there to this day.
en.B: In the middle of the Jordan, Joshua also set up twelve stones, at the spot where the priests carrying the ark of the covenant had stood. They are there to this day.
en.R: Joshua also set up twelve stones out in the middle of the Jordan River, at the place where the priests carrying the ark of the covenant had stood. Those stones are still there today.

sw.L: Na mawe kumi na mawili Yoshua aliyasimamisha katikati ya Yordani, mahali ilipokuwa imesimama miguu ya makuhani waliolibeba sanduku la agano; nayo yamekuwa huko hadi siku hii ya leo.
sw.B: Katikati ya Yordani, Yoshua alisimamisha pia mawe kumi na mawili, mahali walipokuwa wamesimama makuhani waliolibeba sanduku la agano. Yako huko hadi leo.
sw.R: Yoshua alisimamisha pia mawe kumi na mawili katikati ya Mto Yordani, mahali walipokuwa wamesimama makuhani waliolibeba sanduku la agano. Mawe hayo bado yako huko hadi leo.

es.L: Y doce piedras levantó Josué en medio del Jordán, en el lugar donde habían estado los pies de los sacerdotes que llevaban el arca del pacto; y allí están hasta el día de hoy.
es.B: En medio del Jordán, Josué levantó también doce piedras, en el lugar donde habían estado los sacerdotes que llevaban el arca del pacto. Allí están hasta el día de hoy.
es.R: Josué también levantó doce piedras en medio del río Jordán, en el lugar donde habían estado los sacerdotes que llevaban el arca del pacto. Esas piedras todavía están allí hoy.

fr.L: Et douze pierres, Josué [les] dressa au milieu du Jourdain, à l’endroit où s’étaient tenus les pieds des prêtres qui portaient l’arche de l’alliance ; et elles sont là jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.B: Au milieu du Jourdain, Josué dressa aussi douze pierres, à l’endroit où s’étaient tenus les prêtres qui portaient l’arche de l’alliance. Elles y sont encore aujourd’hui.
fr.R: Josué a aussi dressé douze pierres au milieu du Jourdain, à l’endroit où s’étaient tenus les prêtres qui portaient l’arche de l’alliance. Ces pierres sont toujours là aujourd’hui.

vi.L: Và mười hai hòn đá Giô-suê dựng lên giữa sông Giô-đanh, tại chỗ chân các thầy tế lễ khiêng hòm giao ước đã đứng; và chúng vẫn ở đó cho đến ngày nay.
vi.B: Giô-suê cũng dựng mười hai hòn đá ở giữa sông Giô-đanh, tại chỗ các thầy tế lễ khiêng hòm giao ước đã đứng. Các hòn đá ấy vẫn còn ở đó cho đến ngày nay.
vi.R: Giô-suê cũng dựng mười hai hòn đá ngay giữa sông Giô-đanh, tại chỗ các thầy tế lễ khiêng hòm giao ước đã đứng. Những hòn đá ấy vẫn còn ở đó cho đến hôm nay.

ko.L: 그리고 여호수아가 요단 한가운데, 언약궤를 멘 제사장들의 발이 서 있던 곳에 돌 열두 개를 세웠다. 그것들은 오늘까지 거기에 있다.
ko.B: 여호수아는 또 요단강 한가운데, 언약궤를 멘 제사장들이 서 있던 자리에도 돌 열두 개를 세웠다. 그 돌들은 오늘까지 거기에 있다.
ko.R: 여호수아는 또 요단강 한가운데에도 돌 열두 개를 세웠다. 그곳은 언약궤를 멘 제사장들이 서 있던 자리였다. 그 돌들은 오늘날까지 그곳에 있다.

pt.L: E doze pedras Josué levantou no meio do Jordão, no lugar onde estiveram os pés dos sacerdotes que carregavam a arca da aliança; e elas estão ali até este dia.
pt.B: No meio do Jordão, Josué levantou também doze pedras, no lugar onde os sacerdotes que carregavam a arca da aliança tinham ficado. Elas estão lá até hoje.
pt.R: Josué também levantou doze pedras lá no meio do rio Jordão, no lugar onde os sacerdotes que carregavam a arca da aliança tinham ficado. Essas pedras ainda estão lá hoje.

decisions.choice: a second set of twelve stones, set up in the riverbed itself
alternatives: the same twelve stones as in verses 8 and 20, taken from the middle of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The verse says the stones were set up "in the middle of the Jordan", where the priests had stood, while the stones the men carried were set up at Gilgal (verses 8, 20). Putting "twelve stones" first in the sentence suggests a new subject, and the ancient Greek translation reads "other twelve stones". Some take the verse to describe the same stones as verse 8, reading "in the middle of the Jordan" as where they were taken from, but the wording speaks of setting them up in that place.

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the time the book was written
decisions.reason: The phrase is the writer's note that the stones could still be seen in his own time. It comes often in Joshua (5:9; 7:26; 8:28-29).

decisions.choice: also
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "also" to show that this is a second set of stones, as decision m1 explains. Literal keeps the bare Hebrew.

decisions.choice: até este dia (L); até hoje (B); ainda ... hoje (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (5:9; 6:25; 7:26; 8:28-29 and later): the writer's note that something can still be seen (m2) is "até este dia" at Literal, keeping the Hebrew words, and the ordinary "até hoje" at Balanced; Readable says "ainda" with "hoje", as the English Readable says "still".

source.text: וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֞ים נֹשְׂאֵ֣י הָאָר֗וֹן עֹמְדִים֮ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּן֒ עַ֣ד תֹּ֣ם כָּֽל־הַ֠דָּבָר אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־הָעָ֔ם כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ וַיְמַהֲר֥וּ הָעָ֖ם וַֽיַּעֲבֹֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the priests carrying the ark [were] standing in [the] middle of the Jordan until was finished every the thing which commanded Yahweh Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that commanded Moses Joshua; and hurried the people and crossed over.

en.L: And the priests carrying the ark [were] standing in the middle of the Jordan until every thing was finished that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua; and the people hurried and crossed over.
en.B: The priests who carried the ark kept standing in the middle of the Jordan until everything was done that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Joshua to tell the people, just as Moses had commanded Joshua. And the people crossed over in haste.
en.R: The priests carrying the ark stayed in the middle of the Jordan until the people had done everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told Joshua to tell them. It was all just as Moses had told Joshua. The people hurried across the river.

sw.L: Na makuhani waliolibeba sanduku [walikuwa] wamesimama katikati ya Yordani mpaka kila jambo lilipokamilika ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amemwamuru Yoshua kuwaambia watu, sawasawa na yote ambayo Musa alikuwa amemwamuru Yoshua; na watu wakafanya haraka, wakavuka.
sw.B: Makuhani waliolibeba sanduku waliendelea kusimama katikati ya Yordani mpaka kila jambo lilipofanyika ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amemwamuru Yoshua awaambie watu, kama vile Musa alivyokuwa amemwamuru Yoshua. Nao watu wakavuka kwa haraka.
sw.R: Makuhani waliolibeba sanduku walikaa katikati ya Yordani mpaka watu walipomaliza kufanya kila kitu ambacho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Yoshua awaambie. Yote yalikuwa sawasawa na Musa alivyomwambia Yoshua. Watu walivuka mto kwa haraka.

es.L: Y los sacerdotes que llevaban el arca [estaban] de pie en medio del Jordán hasta que se cumplió todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado a Josué que dijera al pueblo, conforme a todo lo que Moisés había mandado a Josué; y el pueblo se apresuró y cruzó.
es.B: Los sacerdotes que llevaban el arca siguieron de pie en medio del Jordán hasta que se cumplió todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado a Josué que dijera al pueblo, tal como Moisés le había mandado a Josué. Y el pueblo cruzó a toda prisa.
es.R: Los sacerdotes que llevaban el arca se quedaron en medio del Jordán hasta que el pueblo hizo todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Josué que les dijera. Todo fue tal como Moisés le había dicho a Josué. El pueblo cruzó el río de prisa.

fr.L: Et les prêtres qui portaient l’arche [se tenaient] debout au milieu du Jourdain jusqu’à ce que fût achevée toute chose que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait commandé à Josué de dire au peuple, selon tout ce que Moïse avait commandé à Josué ; et le peuple se hâta et passa.
fr.B: Les prêtres qui portaient l’arche restèrent debout au milieu du Jourdain jusqu’à ce que soit accompli tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait ordonné à Josué de dire au peuple, comme Moïse l’avait ordonné à Josué. Et le peuple se hâta de traverser.
fr.R: Les prêtres qui portaient l’arche sont restés au milieu du Jourdain jusqu’à ce que le peuple ait fait tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait dit à Josué de leur dire. Tout s’est passé comme Moïse l’avait dit à Josué. Le peuple s’est dépêché de traverser le fleuve.

vi.L: Và các thầy tế lễ khiêng hòm [thì] đứng giữa sông Giô-đanh cho đến khi mọi việc đã xong, là việc {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho Giô-suê nói với dân, theo mọi điều Môi-se đã truyền cho Giô-suê; và dân vội vàng đi qua.
vi.B: Các thầy tế lễ khiêng hòm cứ đứng giữa sông Giô-đanh cho đến khi mọi việc {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho Giô-suê nói với dân được làm xong, đúng như Môi-se đã truyền cho Giô-suê. Và dân vội vàng đi qua sông.
vi.R: Các thầy tế lễ khiêng hòm ở lại giữa sông Giô-đanh cho đến khi dân chúng đã làm xong mọi điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} bảo Giô-suê nói với họ. Mọi việc đều đúng như Môi-se đã dặn Giô-suê. Dân chúng vội vàng đi qua sông.

ko.L: 그리고 그 궤를 멘 제사장들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 여호수아에게 명령하여 백성에게 말하게 하신 모든 일이, 모세가 여호수아에게 명령한 모든 것대로 다 끝날 때까지 요단 한가운데에 서 있었다. 그리고 백성은 서둘러 건너갔다.
ko.B: 그 궤를 멘 제사장들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 여호수아에게 명령하여 백성에게 전하게 하신 모든 일이 다 끝날 때까지 요단강 한가운데에 계속 서 있었다. 모든 것이 모세가 여호수아에게 명령한 그대로였다. 백성은 서둘러 강을 건너갔다.
ko.R: 그 궤를 멘 제사장들은 요단강 한가운데에 그대로 서 있었다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 여호수아에게 백성에게 전하라고 하신 일을 백성이 모두 마칠 때까지 그곳에 있었다. 모든 것이 모세가 여호수아에게 말한 그대로였다. 백성은 서둘러 강을 건넜다.

pt.L: E os sacerdotes que carregavam a arca [estavam] parados no meio do Jordão até que se cumpriu tudo o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha ordenado a Josué que falasse ao povo, conforme tudo o que Moisés tinha ordenado a Josué; e o povo se apressou e atravessou.
pt.B: Os sacerdotes que carregavam a arca continuaram parados no meio do Jordão até que se fez tudo o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha ordenado a Josué que dissesse ao povo, exatamente como Moisés tinha ordenado a Josué. E o povo atravessou depressa.
pt.R: Os sacerdotes que carregavam a arca ficaram no meio do Jordão até que o povo fez tudo o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha mandado Josué dizer a eles. Tudo foi exatamente como Moisés tinha dito a Josué. O povo atravessou o rio depressa.

decisions.choice: every thing: every matter, all that had to be done
decisions.reason: The word can mean "word" or "thing". Here it is everything the LORD had told Joshua to have the people do at the crossing, including the taking of the stones.

decisions.choice: according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua: Moses' charge to Joshua to lead Israel across
decisions.reason: No command of Moses about the details of the crossing is recorded. The phrase points back to the charge Moses gave Joshua to take the people over the Jordan and into the land (Deuteronomy 3:28; 31:7-8, 23), which Joshua is now carrying out.

decisions.choice: the people hurried and crossed over: a look back at the crossing itself
decisions.reason: The verse returns to the people's crossing (3:17; 4:1). It does not say why they hurried; the priests were standing in the riverbed the whole time, holding back the water by the ark.

decisions.choice: It was all just as Moses had told Joshua.
decisions.reason: Readable makes the reference to Moses a short sentence of its own.

source.text: וַיְהִ֛י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־תַּ֥ם כָּל־הָעָ֖ם לַֽעֲב֑וֹר וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר אֲרוֹן־יְהוָ֛ה וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when had finished all the people crossing over, and crossed over [the] ark of Yahweh and the priests before the people.

en.L: And it came about, when all the people had finished crossing over, that the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} crossed over, and the priests, before the people.
en.B: When all the people had finished crossing, the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the priests crossed over in front of the people.
en.R: When all the people were across, the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the priests crossed over too, in front of the people.

sw.L: Ikawa watu wote walipomaliza kuvuka, sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} likavuka, na makuhani, mbele ya watu.
sw.B: Watu wote walipomaliza kuvuka, sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na makuhani walivuka mbele ya watu.
sw.R: Watu wote walipokwisha kuvuka, sanduku la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na makuhani walivuka pia, mbele ya watu.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando todo el pueblo terminó de cruzar, pasó el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y los sacerdotes, delante del pueblo.
es.B: Cuando todo el pueblo terminó de cruzar, el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y los sacerdotes pasaron al otro lado delante del pueblo.
es.R: Cuando todo el pueblo estuvo al otro lado, el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y los sacerdotes también cruzaron, delante del pueblo.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand tout le peuple eut achevé de passer, que l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} passa, ainsi que les prêtres, devant le peuple.
fr.B: Quand tout le peuple eut achevé la traversée, l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et les prêtres passèrent devant le peuple.
fr.R: Quand tout le peuple a été de l’autre côté, l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et les prêtres ont traversé eux aussi, devant le peuple.

vi.L: Và xảy ra, khi cả dân đã đi qua xong, thì hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đi qua, và các thầy tế lễ, trước mặt dân.
vi.B: Khi cả dân đã qua sông xong, hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và các thầy tế lễ đi qua trước mặt dân.
vi.R: Khi toàn dân đã qua sông hết, hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và các thầy tế lễ cũng đi qua, trước mặt dân chúng.

ko.L: 그리고 온 백성이 건너기를 마쳤을 때에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤와 제사장들이 백성 앞에서 건너갔다.
ko.B: 온 백성이 다 건너자, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤와 제사장들이 백성이 보는 앞에서 건너갔다.
ko.R: 백성이 모두 강을 건너자, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 궤와 제사장들도 백성 앞에서 건너왔다.

pt.L: E aconteceu, quando todo o povo acabou de atravessar, que a arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} atravessou, e os sacerdotes, diante do povo.
pt.B: Quando todo o povo terminou de atravessar, a arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e os sacerdotes atravessaram diante do povo.
pt.R: Quando todo o povo já estava do outro lado, a arca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e os sacerdotes também atravessaram, na frente do povo.

decisions.choice: the ark crossed over: a short summary, told in detail in verses 15-18
decisions.reason: The verse tells the end of the crossing in a few words. Verses 15-18 go back and tell how the LORD ordered the priests out of the river and how the water came back.

decisions.choice: before the people: in front of them, in their sight
alternatives: in full view of the people
ahead of the people, at their head
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "in the sight of" the people, who watched the ark come out, or "ahead of" them, as the ark again took its place at the head of the people (3:6). Both fit; the wording is kept open.

source.text: וַ֠יַּעַבְרוּ בְּנֵי־רְאוּבֵ֨ן וּבְנֵי־גָ֜ד וַחֲצִ֨י שֵׁ֤בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁה֙ חֲמֻשִׁ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And crossed over [the] sons of Reuben and [the] sons of Gad and half of [the] tribe of the Manasseh, armed, before [the] sons of Israel, just as had spoken to them Moses.

en.L: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, just as Moses had spoken to them.
en.B: The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh went across armed for battle, ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, as Moses had told them.
en.R: The fighting men from the tribes of Reuben and Gad and from half of the tribe of Manasseh went across ahead of the other {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They were ready for battle, just as Moses had told them to be.

sw.L: Wana wa Reubeni na wana wa Gadi na nusu ya kabila la Manase wakavuka wakiwa wamejipanga kwa vita mbele ya wana wa Israeli, kama Musa alivyowaambia.
sw.B: Wareubeni, Wagadi na nusu ya kabila la Manase walivuka wakiwa na silaha za vita, wakiwatangulia Waisraeli, kama Musa alivyowaambia.
sw.R: Wanaume wa vita kutoka makabila ya Reubeni na Gadi, na kutoka nusu ya kabila la Manase, walivuka wakiwatangulia Waisraeli wengine. Walikuwa tayari kwa vita, kama Musa alivyowaambia.

es.L: Y los hijos de Rubén y los hijos de Gad y la media tribu de Manasés pasaron armados delante de los hijos de Israel, tal como Moisés les había dicho.
es.B: Los rubenitas, los gaditas y la media tribu de Manasés cruzaron armados para la batalla, al frente de los israelitas, como Moisés les había dicho.
es.R: Los guerreros de las tribus de Rubén y de Gad, y de la mitad de la tribu de Manasés, cruzaron delante de los demás israelitas. Estaban listos para la batalla, tal como Moisés les había dicho.

fr.L: Et les fils de Ruben et les fils de Gad et la demi-tribu de Manassé passèrent en armes devant les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, comme Moïse le leur avait dit.
fr.B: Les Rubénites, les Gadites et la demi-tribu de Manassé traversèrent armés pour le combat, devant les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, comme Moïse le leur avait dit.
fr.R: Les guerriers des tribus de Ruben et de Gad et de la moitié de la tribu de Manassé ont traversé devant les autres {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Ils étaient prêts pour la bataille, comme Moïse le leur avait demandé.

vi.L: Và con cháu Ru-bên, con cháu Gát và nửa chi tộc Ma-na-se, vũ trang, đi qua trước con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên, đúng như Môi-se đã phán dặn họ.
vi.B: Người Ru-bên, người Gát và nửa chi tộc Ma-na-se vũ trang sẵn sàng chiến đấu, đi qua trước dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, như Môi-se đã dặn họ.
vi.R: Các chiến sĩ của chi tộc Ru-bên, chi tộc Gát và nửa chi tộc Ma-na-se đi qua sông trước những người Y-sơ-ra-ên khác. Họ đã sẵn sàng chiến đấu, đúng như Môi-se đã dặn họ.

ko.L: 그리고 르우벤 자손과 갓 자손과 므낫세 지파의 절반이 모세가 그들에게 말한 대로 무장하고 이스라엘 자손 앞에서 건너갔다.
ko.B: 르우벤 지파와 갓 지파와 므낫세 반 지파는 모세가 그들에게 말한 대로 싸울 준비를 갖추고 이스라엘 자손보다 앞서 건너갔다.
ko.R: 르우벤 지파와 갓 지파와 므낫세 지파의 절반에서 온 군인들이 다른 이스라엘 백성보다 앞서 강을 건넜다. 모세가 그들에게 말한 대로, 그들은 싸울 준비를 갖추고 있었다.

pt.L: E os filhos de Rúben, e os filhos de Gade, e a meia tribo de Manassés atravessaram armados diante dos filhos de Israel, como Moisés lhes tinha falado.
pt.B: Os rubenitas, os gaditas e a meia tribo de Manassés atravessaram armados para a batalha, à frente dos israelitas, como Moisés lhes tinha dito.
pt.R: Os soldados das tribos de Rúben e de Gade e da metade da tribo de Manassés atravessaram à frente dos outros israelitas. Eles estavam prontos para a batalha, exatamente como Moisés tinha mandado.

decisions.choice: just as Moses had spoken to them: the promise of the tribes that settled east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh received land east of the Jordan on one condition: their fighting men would cross ahead of the other tribes and fight until the whole land was taken (Numbers 32:20-32; Deuteronomy 3:18-20). Joshua reminded them of it before the crossing (1:12-18), and here they keep their word.

decisions.choice: armed: ready for war, perhaps drawn up in battle order
decisions.reason: The word is used of Israel leaving Egypt "armed" or "in battle array" (Exodus 13:18) and of these same tribes in 1:14. Its exact sense is not certain: it may mean equipped for battle, or marching in ranks. Either way they crossed as soldiers.

decisions.choice: the sons of Reuben and of Gad: their fighting men
decisions.reason: The verse means the warriors of these tribes, not the whole tribes. Their families and herds stayed on the east side (1:14; Numbers 32:26-27), and verse 13 gives their number.

decisions.choice: the Reubenites, the Gadites (Balanced); the fighting men from the tribes (Readable)
decisions.reason: These are men of war, so no gender setting applies. Balanced uses the tribe names, as Numbers 32 does; Readable says plainly that the fighting men are meant.

source.text: כְּאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף חֲלוּצֵ֣י הַצָּבָ֑א עָבְר֞וּ לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה אֶ֖ל עַֽרְב֥וֹת יְרִיחֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: About forty thousand equipped [for] the army crossed over before Yahweh for the battle, to [the] plains of Jericho.

en.L: About 40,000 equipped for the army crossed over before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for battle, to the plains of Jericho.
en.B: About 40,000 men equipped for war crossed over before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, ready for battle, to the plains of Jericho.
en.R: About 40,000 soldiers went across in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the plains near Jericho. They were armed and ready to fight.

sw.L: Kama elfu arobaini waliojiandaa kwa jeshi walivuka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa vita, hadi nchi tambarare za Yeriko.
sw.B: Wanaume kama elfu arobaini waliojiandaa kwa vita walivuka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, tayari kwa mapigano, hadi nchi tambarare za Yeriko.
sw.R: Askari kama elfu arobaini walivuka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hadi nchi tambarare karibu na Yeriko. Walikuwa na silaha, tayari kupigana.

es.L: Unos 40 000 equipados para el ejército pasaron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} para la batalla, a las llanuras de Jericó.
es.B: Unos 40 000 hombres equipados para la guerra pasaron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, listos para la batalla, a las llanuras de Jericó.
es.R: Unos 40 000 soldados cruzaron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} hasta las llanuras cercanas a Jericó. Iban armados y listos para pelear.

fr.L: Environ quarante mille équipés pour l’armée passèrent devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pour la bataille, vers les plaines de Jéricho.
fr.B: Environ 40 000 hommes équipés pour la guerre passèrent devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, prêts au combat, vers les plaines de Jéricho.
fr.R: Environ 40 000 soldats ont traversé devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} jusqu’aux plaines près de Jéricho. Ils étaient armés et prêts à se battre.

vi.L: Chừng 40.000 [người] được trang bị cho quân đội đi qua trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} để chiến đấu, đến các đồng bằng Giê-ri-cô.
vi.B: Chừng 40.000 người được trang bị để chiến đấu đi qua trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, sẵn sàng ra trận, đến các đồng bằng Giê-ri-cô.
vi.R: Chừng 40.000 người lính đi qua trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đến vùng đồng bằng gần Giê-ri-cô. Họ đã được trang bị vũ khí và sẵn sàng chiến đấu.

ko.L: 군대를 위해 무장한 사만 명쯤이 싸우러 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 여리고 평지로 건너갔다.
ko.B: 싸울 준비를 갖춘 사만 명쯤 되는 군사들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 건너가 여리고 평지로 나아가 전투에 대비했다.
ko.R: 군인 사만 명쯤이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 강을 건너 여리고 근처의 평지로 갔다. 그들은 무기를 갖추고 싸울 준비가 되어 있었다.

pt.L: Cerca de 40.000 equipados para a guerra atravessaram diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} para a batalha, para as planícies de Jericó.
pt.B: Cerca de 40.000 homens equipados para a guerra atravessaram diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, prontos para a batalha, para as planícies de Jericó.
pt.R: Cerca de 40.000 soldados atravessaram diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} até as planícies perto de Jericó. Eles estavam armados e prontos para lutar.

decisions.choice: about forty thousand: the part of the eastern tribes' fighting men who crossed
decisions.reason: The census on the plains of Moab counted over 110,000 men of fighting age in Reuben, Gad and the whole of Manasseh (Numbers 26:7, 18, 34). Forty thousand were sent over; others stayed behind with the families and herds (Numbers 32:16-17). On the size of the word "thousand", see the note at Numbers 1:21.

decisions.choice: equipped for the army: men armed and ready for war
decisions.reason: The word describes men stripped for action and armed (Numbers 32:21, 27, 29). Joined to the word for an army, it means men fit and equipped for military service.

decisions.choice: before the LORD: in the presence of the LORD, whose ark went with them
decisions.reason: The ark was the sign of the LORD's presence among his people (3:10-11). To march "before the LORD" is to go out under his eye and at his command; the battle is his (5:13-15; 6:2).

decisions.choice: the plains of Jericho: the flat floor of the Jordan valley around the city
decisions.reason: The valley west of the river is a wide, low plain. Jericho, an oasis city, stood at its western edge, about five miles from the river.

decisions.choice: men (Balanced); soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "equipped ones" has no noun. Balanced and Readable supply one, since these are the fighting men of verse 12.

records.literal_gloss: On the day the that made great Yahweh Joshua in [the] eyes of all Israel; and they feared him just as they had feared Moses, all [the] days of his life.

en.L: On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they feared him, just as they had feared Moses, all the days of his life.
en.B: That day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} raised Joshua up in the sight of all Israel, and they held him in awe all his life, just as they had held Moses in awe.
en.R: That day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made all Israel see how great a leader Joshua was. They respected him deeply for as long as he lived, just as they had respected Moses.

sw.L: Siku hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimtukuza Yoshua machoni pa Israeli wote, nao wakamcha, kama walivyomcha Musa, siku zote za maisha yake.
sw.B: Siku hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwinua Yoshua machoni pa Israeli wote, nao wakamheshimu kwa kicho maisha yake yote, kama walivyomheshimu Musa.
sw.R: Siku hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaonyesha Israeli wote jinsi Yoshua alivyokuwa kiongozi mkuu. Walimheshimu sana maisha yake yote, kama walivyomheshimu Musa.

es.L: Aquel día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} engrandeció a Josué a los ojos de todo Israel, y lo temieron, como habían temido a Moisés, todos los días de su vida.
es.B: Aquel día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} enalteció a Josué a la vista de todo Israel, y lo reverenciaron toda su vida, como habían reverenciado a Moisés.
es.R: Aquel día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo que todo Israel viera qué gran líder era Josué. Lo respetaron profundamente mientras vivió, como habían respetado a Moisés.

fr.L: En ce jour-là, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} grandit Josué aux yeux de tout Israël, et ils le craignirent comme ils avaient craint Moïse, tous les jours de sa vie.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} éleva Josué aux yeux de tout Israël, et on le respecta avec crainte toute sa vie, comme on avait respecté Moïse.
fr.R: Ce jour-là, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a montré à tout Israël quel grand chef était Josué. Le peuple l’a profondément respecté tant qu’il a vécu, comme il avait respecté Moïse.

vi.L: Trong ngày ấy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm cho Giô-suê được tôn trọng trước mắt cả Y-sơ-ra-ên, và họ kính sợ ông như đã kính sợ Môi-se, trọn mọi ngày của đời ông.
vi.B: Ngày hôm ấy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tôn Giô-suê lên trước mắt cả Y-sơ-ra-ên, và họ kính sợ ông suốt đời ông, như đã kính sợ Môi-se.
vi.R: Ngày hôm ấy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm cho cả Y-sơ-ra-ên thấy Giô-suê là một người lãnh đạo lớn. Họ hết lòng kính trọng ông suốt cuộc đời ông, như họ đã kính trọng Môi-se.

ko.L: 그날에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 온 이스라엘의 눈앞에서 여호수아를 크게 하셨다. 그래서 그들은 모세를 두려워한 것처럼 여호수아가 사는 모든 날 동안 그를 두려워했다.
ko.B: 그날 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 온 이스라엘이 보는 앞에서 여호수아를 높이셨다. 그래서 그들은 모세를 경외했던 것처럼 여호수아가 사는 동안 내내 그를 경외했다.
ko.R: 그날 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 여호수아가 얼마나 큰 지도자인지 온 이스라엘이 보게 하셨다. 그래서 백성은 모세를 깊이 존경했던 것처럼, 여호수아가 살아 있는 동안 내내 그를 깊이 존경했다.

pt.L: Naquele dia {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} engrandeceu Josué aos olhos de todo o Israel; e eles o temeram, como tinham temido Moisés, todos os dias da sua vida.
pt.B: Naquele dia {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} exaltou Josué diante de todo o Israel, e eles o respeitaram com temor durante toda a vida dele, como tinham respeitado Moisés.
pt.R: Naquele dia {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} fez todo o Israel ver como Josué era um grande líder. Eles o respeitaram muito enquanto ele viveu, como tinham respeitado Moisés.

decisions.choice: the LORD made Joshua great: the promise of 3:7 kept
decisions.reason: Before the crossing the LORD said, "Today I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel, so that they may know that as I was with Moses, I will be with you" (3:7). The parting of the Jordan, like the parting of the sea under Moses (Exodus 14:31), shows the people that God stands behind their leader.

decisions.choice: feared: held in awe and respected as God's chosen leader
decisions.reason: The verb means "to fear", but said of people toward a leader God has set over them it means deep respect and readiness to obey, not terror. After the sea, Israel "feared the LORD and believed in the LORD and in his servant Moses" (Exodus 14:31).

decisions.choice: all the days of his life: Joshua's life
alternatives: just as they had feared Moses all the days of Moses' life
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew the phrase comes after "Moses", so it could mean that Israel feared Moses all his life. But the point of the verse is how Joshua was regarded from that day on, and the phrase is taken with "they feared him".

decisions.choice: made all Israel see how great a leader Joshua was; respected him deeply
decisions.reason: Readable explains "made great in the eyes of" and puts "feared" as deep respect, which is the sense here (decision m2).

decisions.choice: the story goes back to the moment before the ark came up
decisions.reason: Verse 11 has already said that the ark crossed. Verses 15-18 now tell how it happened: the LORD gave the order, Joshua passed it on, and the water returned as the priests stepped out.

en.B: "Order the priests carrying the ark of the testimony to come up from the Jordan."
en.R: "Tell the priests carrying the ark that holds the covenant tablets to come up out of the Jordan."

sw.R: "Waambie makuhani wanaolibeba sanduku lenye vibao vya mawe vya agano watoke ndani ya Yordani."

es.R: «Diles a los sacerdotes que llevan el arca que guarda las tablas del pacto que salgan del Jordán».

ko.L: "증거궤를 멘 제사장들에게 명령하여 요단에서 올라오게 하여라."
ko.B: "증거궤를 멘 제사장들에게 요단강에서 올라오라고 명령하여라."
ko.R: "언약의 돌판을 넣어 둔 궤를 멘 제사장들에게 요단강에서 올라오라고 말하여라."

pt.B: "Dá ordem aos sacerdotes que carregam a arca do Testemunho que saiam do Jordão."
pt.R: "Manda os sacerdotes que carregam a arca com as tábuas da aliança saírem do Jordão."

decisions.choice: the ark of the testimony: the ark that held the tablets of the covenant
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the name for the two stone tablets of the covenant, which were kept in the ark (Exodus 25:16, 21-22; 31:18). This is the only place in Joshua that uses this name for the ark; elsewhere in these chapters it is "the ark of the covenant".

decisions.choice: the ark that holds the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable explains "testimony", as it does in Exodus, so young readers know what is meant.

decisions.choice: "hòm chứng ước" (L, B), "chiếc hòm đựng các bảng đá giao ước" (R)
decisions.reason: A second name for the ark, "the ark of the testimony", meaning the tablets of the covenant inside it (m1). "chứng ước" keeps it apart from "hòm giao ước"; Readable says what it was.

decisions.choice: "증거궤" for "the ark of the testimony" (L, B)
alternatives: "언약궤", the name used elsewhere in the chapter
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a different name here, after the tablets of the testimony the ark held. Literal and Balanced keep it; Readable says what it was, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: a arca do Testemunho (L, B); a arca com as tábuas da aliança (R)
decisions.reason: As docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md sets it: "o Testemunho", with a capital, names the tablets of the covenant (m1); Readable says what they are, as the English Readable does.

es.R: Entonces Josué les dio la orden a los sacerdotes: «{{plural_you:Salgan|Salid}} del Jordán».

fr.B: Josué donna donc cet ordre aux prêtres : « Remontez du Jourdain. »
fr.R: Josué a donc donné cet ordre aux prêtres : « Sortez du Jourdain. »

ko.R: 그래서 여호수아가 제사장들에게 명령을 내렸다. "요단강에서 올라오너라."

pt.R: Então Josué deu esta ordem aos sacerdotes: "Saiam do Jordão."

decisions.choice: Joshua passes on the LORD's word as it was given
decisions.reason: The priests move only when the LORD gives the word through Joshua. The order in verse 16 and Joshua's command here use the same verb, "come up", so his word is shown to be the LORD's word.

source.text: וַ֠יְהִי כַּעֲל֨וֹת הַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים נֹשְׂאֵ֨י אֲר֤וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָה֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן נִתְּק֗וּ כַּפּוֹת֙ רַגְלֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים אֶ֖ל הֶחָרָבָ֑ה וַיָּשֻׁ֤בוּ מֵֽי־הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ לִמְקוֹמָ֔ם וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ כִתְמוֹל־שִׁלְשׁ֖וֹם עַל־כָּל־גְּדוֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as came up the priests carrying [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh from [the] middle of the Jordan, were drawn out [the] soles of [the] feet of the priests to the dry ground, and returned [the] waters of the Jordan to their place and went as yesterday [and] three days ago over all its banks.

en.L: And it came about, as the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came up from the middle of the Jordan, [and] the soles of the feet of the priests were pulled up onto the dry ground, that the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and went as before over all its banks.
en.B: As the priests who carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stepped up from the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of their feet came out onto dry ground, the Jordan's waters went back to their place and flowed over all its banks as they had before.
en.R: The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} climbed up out of the middle of the river. As soon as their feet stepped up onto dry ground, the water of the Jordan came back. It flowed over all its banks again, just as it had before.

sw.L: Ikawa makuhani waliolibeba sanduku la agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} walipopanda kutoka katikati ya Yordani, [na] nyayo za miguu ya makuhani zilipoinuliwa kwenye nchi kavu, maji ya Yordani yakarudi mahali pake, yakaenda kama zamani juu ya kingo zake zote.
sw.B: Makuhani waliolibeba sanduku la agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} walipopanda kutoka katikati ya Yordani, na nyayo za miguu yao zilipofika nchi kavu, maji ya Yordani yalirudi mahali pake, yakafurika kingo zake zote kama hapo awali.
sw.R: Makuhani waliolibeba sanduku la agano la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} walipanda kutoka katikati ya mto. Mara miguu yao ilipokanyaga nchi kavu, maji ya Yordani yalirudi. Yakafurika tena kingo zake zote, kama ilivyokuwa kabla.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando los sacerdotes que llevaban el arca del pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} subieron de en medio del Jordán, [y] las plantas de los pies de los sacerdotes se alzaron sobre la tierra seca, las aguas del Jordán volvieron a su lugar y corrieron como antes por encima de todas sus riberas.
es.B: Cuando los sacerdotes que llevaban el arca del pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} subieron de en medio del Jordán y las plantas de sus pies salieron a tierra seca, las aguas del Jordán volvieron a su lugar y se desbordaron por todas sus riberas como antes.
es.R: Los sacerdotes que llevaban el arca del pacto {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} salieron de en medio del río. En cuanto sus pies pisaron tierra seca, el agua del Jordán volvió. Se desbordó otra vez por todas sus orillas, igual que antes.

fr.L: Et il arriva, comme les prêtres qui portaient l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} montaient du milieu du Jourdain, [et que] les plantes des pieds des prêtres se posaient sur la terre sèche, que les eaux du Jourdain retournèrent à leur place et coulèrent comme auparavant par-dessus toutes ses rives.
fr.B: Au moment où les prêtres qui portaient l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} remontèrent du milieu du Jourdain et où la plante de leurs pieds se posa sur la terre sèche, les eaux du Jourdain revinrent à leur place et débordèrent sur toutes ses rives comme auparavant.
fr.R: Les prêtres qui portaient l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sont remontés du milieu du fleuve. Dès que leurs pieds ont touché la terre sèche, l’eau du Jourdain est revenue. Elle a de nouveau débordé sur toutes ses rives, comme avant.

vi.L: Và xảy ra, khi các thầy tế lễ khiêng hòm giao ước của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đi lên từ giữa sông Giô-đanh, [và] bàn chân các thầy tế lễ vừa nhấc lên đặt trên đất khô, thì nước sông Giô-đanh trở lại chỗ cũ và chảy tràn khắp bờ như trước.
vi.B: Khi các thầy tế lễ khiêng hòm giao ước của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} bước lên từ giữa sông Giô-đanh, và bàn chân họ vừa đặt lên đất khô, thì nước sông Giô-đanh trở lại chỗ cũ và chảy tràn khắp bờ như trước.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 언약궤를 멘 제사장들이 요단 한가운데에서 올라와, 제사장들의 발바닥이 마른 땅으로 들려 올라섰을 때에, 요단 물이 제자리로 돌아와 전처럼 모든 둑에 넘쳐흘렀다.

decisions.choice: the soles of the feet were pulled up onto the dry ground: the priests stepped out of the riverbed onto the bank
decisions.reason: The verb means "to be pulled away" or "torn loose", as a foot is pulled free from the ground. The priests had stood in the riverbed from the start (3:15-17); the moment their feet came up out of it onto the dry ground, the river returned. The same feet that stopped the water when they touched it (3:13, 15) let it go when they left.

decisions.choice: as yesterday and the day before: as it had before
decisions.reason: "Yesterday and the day before" means "formerly", "as usual" (Genesis 31:2; Exodus 5:7).

decisions.choice: over all its banks: in spring flood
decisions.reason: The crossing took place at harvest time, when the Jordan overflows its banks (3:15) from the rains and the melting snow of Mount Hermon. The return of the flood shows that the dry crossing had been God's doing, not a low river.

decisions.choice: [and]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the two clauses about the priests side by side. Literal supplies "and" in brackets so the long sentence can be followed.

decisions.choice: as before / as they had before / just as it had before
decisions.reason: The idiom is given by its meaning at every level, since "as yesterday and three days ago" would mislead in English. The literal gloss keeps the Hebrew words.

decisions.choice: the tenth of the first month: the day the Passover lamb was chosen, forty years after the exodus

On its tenth day each household chose its lamb (Exodus 12:3), and four days later Israel kept the Passover at Gilgal (5:10). The people left Egypt in this month (Numbers 33:3) and now enter the land in it, forty years on (5:6).

decisions.choice: Gilgal: Israel's first camp in the land, between the Jordan and Jericho
decisions.reason: The site is not known for certain. It became the base camp for the early campaigns (9:6; 10:6) and a holy place in later times (1 Samuel 11:14-15). The name sounds like the verb "to roll", which 5:9 explains.

decisions.choice: the eastern edge of Jericho: the east side of the city's territory
decisions.reason: "Jericho" here means the city with its lands. Gilgal lay at their eastern edge, toward the river.

decisions.choice: the tenth day
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "the tenth of the month"; Balanced and Readable add "day", as English dates require.

decisions.choice: "Guilgal"

decisions.choice: "ngày mồng mười tháng giêng" (L, B), "ngày mười tháng thứ nhất" (R)
decisions.reason: "tháng giêng" is the usual name for the first month of the year; Readable says "the first month" in the plainest words, since some readers may hear "tháng giêng" as January or the lunar new year month.

decisions.choice: the answer to the children ends with verse 22; verses 23-24 are Joshua's words to Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no quotation marks. Verse 23 begins "for" and speaks of what God did "before you ... until you crossed", which fits Joshua speaking to those who had just crossed. The words could also be heard as part of what the parents are to tell their children.

decisions.choice: just as ... to the Sea of Reeds: the crossing of the sea out of Egypt
decisions.reason: The LORD drove back the sea and made it dry land, and Israel went through on dry ground (Exodus 14:21-22). The Jordan crossing repeats that wonder for the generation entering the land.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the sea Israel crossed out of Egypt
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name means "sea of reeds". It is the sea of the exodus (Exodus 15:4) and is also used of the Gulf of Aqaba (1 Kings 9:26). Its exact location for the crossing is not certain.

decisions.choice: before us ... we: Joshua counts himself among those who crossed the sea
decisions.reason: Joshua had come out of Egypt as a young man (Exodus 17:9; 33:11; Numbers 14:30). He says "we" of the sea and "you" of the Jordan, and so joins the two generations in one story.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea (Balanced, Readable); the Sea of Reeds (Literal)
decisions.reason: Literal gives the Hebrew name. Balanced and Readable use the name known to most readers, as Exodus 15:4 does.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD: his power at work
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power and action. The phrase recalls the exodus, when the LORD brought Israel out "with a mighty hand" (Exodus 13:9; Deuteronomy 4:34).

decisions.choice: two purposes: that the nations may know, and that Israel may fear
decisions.reason: The wonder is for the whole world to see as well as for Israel. The peoples of Canaan had already heard of the sea (2:9-11) and now hear of the Jordan (5:1). For Israel the purpose is lasting reverence for God.

decisions.choice: so that you may fear: Israel is the one who is to fear
alternatives: so that they [the peoples] may fear the LORD your God
decisions.reason: The verb form in the Hebrew is unusual after "so that". With a small change of its vowels it would read "so that they may fear", carrying on the subject "all the peoples of the earth". The text as written says "you", and that is followed here.

decisions.choice: fear the LORD all the days: revere and obey him always
decisions.reason: To fear the LORD is to stand in awe of him and so to keep his commands (Deuteronomy 6:2, 13, 24). "All the days" means for all time.

decisions.choice: He did this
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence here and so supplies its subject, the LORD of verse 23.

decisions.choice: how powerful the LORD is; stand in awe of
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the mighty hand and keeps the sense of "fear" as reverence, not terror (decision m4).
